diagram_math_checks.result: A and B are the stated intended-link bounds, and C is exactly the minimum of the two receiver sum bounds. The local channel definition has Y1=h11 X1+h21 X2+Z1, Y2=h12 X1+h22 X2+Z2; thus INR1=|h21|^2 P2 and INR2=|h12|^2 P1. No gain indices are swapped.
|h12|>=|h11| implies INR2>=SNR1 and |h21|>=|h22| implies INR1>=SNR2. Each logarithmic sum bound is consequently at least both A and B; kappa>0 gives C>=max(A,B).
diagram_math_checks.basis: Carrier Statement strong inequalities; local Definition SNR/INR conventions.

diagram_math_checks.check: Five boundary edges and shaded side
diagram_math_checks.result: For A,B>0 and max(A,B)<C<A+B the five vertices are (0,0),(A,0),(A,C-A),(C-B,B),(0,B). Both cut endpoints lie strictly on their respective rectangle edges. Their coordinate sums are C, so the sloping edge has slope -1 and the shaded side contains the origin. The actual rendering shows all five boundary edges including the explicit last-to-first closure, plus two dashed edges completing the rectangle.
diagram_math_checks.basis: Intersection of the three exact Statement bounds with nonnegative rates; Remarks lines 73-75 and TikZ lines 79-88.

diagram_math_checks.result: C>=A+B retains the whole rectangle, including equality. At C=max(A,B)<A+B one endpoint reaches an axis; if A=B=C both do and the region is triangular. If A=0 or B=0, C>=max(A,B) leaves exactly the corresponding axis segment; if both vanish it is the origin. In particular h21=0 forces h22=0 and B=0, while h12=0 forces h11=0 and A=0, consistent with proof 3.1.
